transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Hill (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Stratus Labs - Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Stratus Labs - CTO), Miguel Ortega (Stratus Labs - Platform Lead)
Recording id: ff-20260910-8243

Summary (auto):
Redwood walkthrough focused on migration parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to the Redwood API. SE demo covered API call mapping, streaming, function/tool calling equivalents, token cost estimation, and infra options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Security questions raised around SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS and audit logs. Agreed next steps: shared parity spreadsheet, pricing, POC kickoff.

Topics: 
- Parity mapping for completions/chat/embeddings/rerank
- Streaming & function-calling equivalents
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching, KV cache
- Deployment modes: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, SSO, audit logs, data residency
- POC/benchmark plan and sample prompts

Action items (auto in transcript): see metadata action_items

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everybody thanks for joining, we'll give a migration demo today focusing on parity with OpenAI, Anthropic and Together, and then Marcus will run through the SE bits.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Hey Lena, thanks. Quick note we have 45 minutes, Tom's got another call at 15:50 so we'll try to be efficient.
[00:20] Lena Park: Perfect, we'll aim for a 35-minute demo and 10 for Q&A. Marcus over to you for the tech map.
[00:27] Marcus Hill: Cool thanks Lena. Hi team at Stratus. So outline: I'll show equivalent Redwood API calls for text-gen/chat, embeddings and reranking, then show console for routing and Optimize suggestions.
[00:38] Tom Reynolds: Great, our main goals are parity in outputs, predictable latency under 200ms p50 for short prompts, and cost that's not explosive. Also we have strict data residency needs for EU traffic.
[00:50] Marcus Hill: Understood. We'll show both hosted and Dedicated options; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and private networking for compliance. For parity: Redwood supports chat primitives, streaming, function/tool calling equivalents — sometimes names differ but semantics match.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: When you say 'function calling equivalents' can you map to the Anthropic tool call pattern? We have a lot of JSON-schema based outputs.
[01:12] Marcus Hill: Yes, we support structured output and schema enforcement in the SDK. For Anthropic-style tool calls, the Redwood approach is the same conceptually — you'll receive a structured payload, we can validate against schema and route to your microservices. Slight differences in field names may require a thin adapter. We'll include mapping in the parity sheet.
[01:30] Miguel Ortega: Any gotchas with streaming? We use streaming for progressive UI updates and low-latency tokens.
[01:36] Marcus Hill: Streaming is first-class. You can stream tokens back over the Redwood REST/SDK. Under the hood for long-running state we manage KV cache and prefix caching to reduce token compute. There can be differences in chunking/flush behaviour versus OpenAI — we'll show an example.
[01:50] Speaker 1: so uh we had some issues before where tokens weren't flushed until the full response, is that right
[01:55] Marcus Hill: Yeah, good point. Redwood's streaming flushes incrementally; latency depends on your min_tokens and server side batching. Optimize has suggestions to tune batching for latency-sensitive UIs.
[02:10] Lena Park: I'll pull up the parity mapping doc and a sample prompt. Marcus, can you show the API example?
[02:20] Marcus Hill: Sure. Example: OpenAI completion -> Redwood text.generate call. Chat completion -> chat.create with messages array. For Together prompt format we have a compatibility layer. For embeddings: same vector endpoint with model param mapping.
[02:34] Tom Reynolds: How about tokenization differences? We rely on token-level cost forecasts.
[02:38] Marcus Hill: Tokenizers can differ; we provide tokenizers in the SDK aligned to each model variant and we'll estimate cost per-model in the parity sheet. Expect small delta between vendors but we can run a sample set to quantify.
[02:54] Aisha Khan: Security — do you have SOC 2 Type II and can we integrate with our KMS? We're also required to have audit logs for model inputs for a subset of customers.
[03:02] Lena Park: Yes SOC 2 is available; for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs. For hosted, we can enable additional retention and logs as an add-on — we'll include the compliance pack in pricing.
[03:18] Tom Reynolds: For EU data residency, does Redwood have region controls or do we need Private?
[03:24] Marcus Hill: Hosted supports region routing for EU regions. If you require strict VPC-only control or on-prem, Dedicated or Private is the path. We'll recommend Dedicated in your case for predictable SLAs and region isolation.
[03:36] Miguel Ortega: Any requirement changes for model sizes when migrating? We used gpt-like models from OpenAI and Claude from Anthropic for assistant and Together for specialized smaller models.
[03:46] Marcus Hill: We'll map model families to Redwood-verified variants. For example, small request routing -> quantized variants on Dedicated to save cost. For high-quality assistants we map to full-precision variants. The Optimize module recommends quantization and batching settings by workload.
[04:05] Aisha Khan: Can you demo the Console Optimize recommendations?
[04:10] Marcus Hill: Sure, switching screens. In the console you get per-route latency/cost; Optimize surfaces suggested batch sizes, KV cache TTLs and quantization profiles. For example, we recommended batching=8 for your expected 45% short-turn prompts to hit the 200ms p50 and reduce cost ~20%. These are suggestions you can apply cluster-wide or per-route.
[04:34] Speaker 2: there's a note about auto fallback to cheaper variants - how does that affect output quality
[04:38] Marcus Hill: Good question. We allow automatic fallback with quality thresholds. If the cheaper variant's output diverges on evals, the route will fall back to the higher-quality model. We tie regressions to prompt eval sets so you can detect quality drop.
[04:55] Tom Reynolds: About SLAs — what's included on Dedicated?
[05:00] Lena Park: Dedicated includes uptime SLAs, latency SLOs, and priority support. We'll include exact numbers in the contract template.
[05:06] Aisha Khan: Let's talk costs — can you ballpark for our traffic? We currently spend about $40k/mo across providers, aim to keep under $30k with better batching.
[05:15] Marcus Hill: We'll run numbers in the parity sheet. Preliminary: with batching, KV cache and quantized variants we usually see 15-30% reduction in unit costs depending on your prompt distribution. We'll attach a sample calc.
[05:32] Miguel Ortega: For POC, what does the SE need from us?
[05:36] Marcus Hill: Sample prompt set, traffic profile (requests per second, percent of short vs long prompts), expected p50/p95 SLOs, and one or two representative dataset examples for embeddings. If you can grant a sandbox API key and sample logs that's ideal.
[05:52] Lena Park: I'll add that to next steps. We'll also share a link to the migration deck and parity spreadsheet.
[05:58] Marcus Hill: Demo note: there are small transcription variances for model names in some logs we ingest, so mapping may need manual checks.
[06:07] Aisha Khan: On security again, how do you handle model input data retention for audit requests?
[06:12] Marcus Hill: We can configure retention policies per-customer and per-route. For hosted we retain minimal logs by default; for compliance you can enable long-term retention with encrypted logs and KMS control. Private gives you full control.
[06:27] Tom Reynolds: OK. Let's walk through a short live migration example — take a Together prompt -> Redwood call and compare output.
[06:34] Marcus Hill: Live example: sending Together prompt X. (typing) Redwood returns earlier due to prefix cache. Output: "Hey Tom, here's a concise summary..." You can see differences in phrasing but semantically similar. We'll run batch parity tests for BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and human evals.
[06:58] Miguel Ortega: How do you version models and roll out safely?
[07:03] Marcus Hill: Console supports canary rollouts, A/B testing, automatic fallbacks and traffic splitting. You can pin model versions and then promote after eval pass. Logs and diffing tools help track regressions.
[07:18] Aisha Khan: Do you support SSO/SAML for RBAC?
[07:22] Lena Park: Yes. SSO, SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC are supported. We also offer audit logs for workspace and API activity.
[07:33] Tom Reynolds: Any limitations on inference plugins or custom kernels for on-prem?
[07:38] Marcus Hill: For Private on-prem customers we can integrate custom kernels and collab with your infra team; it's part of the enterprise engagement.
[07:47] Lena Park: Quick recap — we'll send parity mapping, pricing, and set up SE-led POC. Anything else?
[07:54] Aisha Khan: Please include a sample SLA for Dedicated and a checklist for SOC2 evidence.
[07:59] Lena Park: Will do. Marcus, last note on benchmarks?
[08:03] Marcus Hill: We'll run a 1-week benchmark with your sample prompts in our sandbox, measuring latency, p50/p95, and token cost. We'll share raw logs and a summary.
[08:14] Tom Reynolds: Sounds good. If POC looks acceptable, procurement will need a standard contract and data processing addendum.
[08:21] Lena Park: We'll attach the DPA and contract template with pricing.
[08:24] Miguel Ortega: One nit — are there SDK differences that will force changes to our code paths? We want minimal adapter work.
[08:30] Marcus Hill: Mostly thin adapters. Chat/message arrays map naturally. Function-calling schema might need small transforms. We'll include code snippets in the parity doc and a migration guide.
[08:43] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[08:46] Marcus Hill: Also note Optimize can do per-route suggestions automatically; you can export suggestions as a config.
[08:54] Lena Park: Okay let's move to Q&A and remaining concerns.
[08:58] Aisha Khan: Are there any known regression risks when moving from Anthropic to Redwood models for safety/guardrails?
[09:05] Marcus Hill: We run safety filters and provide guardrail configs. If a model variant shows different behavior, the eval framework flags it. For high-sensitivity use cases we recommend composing filters and fallback policies.
[09:18] Tom Reynolds: For embeddings, how do we ensure vector parity and indexing compatibility?
[09:23] Marcus Hill: We provide tokenizer and embedder parity tests; typically you reindex in the POC, but we offer migration tooling and export helpers. We'll show a sample script.
[09:36] Aisha Khan: Ok I think that's all from us.
[09:40] Lena Park: Great. Quick recap of next steps, Marcus?
[09:43] Marcus Hill: I'll send parity mapping, run an initial token-cost calc, and schedule the POC kickoff. Lena will send pricing and DPA. Customer to send prompts and logs.
[09:54] Tom Reynolds: Thanks everyone.
[09:56] Lena Park: Thanks all. We'll target those due dates and follow up in email with links (parity spreadsheet, deck: https://redwood.ai/deck/migration-parity).
[10:05] End of recording
